review_notes: I read the whole target file. It declares no simp lemmas or attributes of its own, so I looked at which simp-relevant lemmas it uses and how. I also read the defining files in CubicGram (Reciprocity.lean, ResidueCharacters.lean, PrimaryNormalization.lean). Most `simp` calls in the target are ordinary closers, and I found no cycles or competing rules. The one concrete gap I found is that `cubicSymbol_one_lower` is an unconditional, terminating rewrite with no simp attribute, and callers have to pass it by hand. That finding rests on the lemma's definition and its call sites. I did not run Lean, and I did not check how a global simp tag would interact with other `cubicSymbol` rules in files that import it. Smaller observations I chose not to report: `show omega ^ (3 : ℤ) = 1 by simpa using omega_cube` appears twice (lines 152 and 176), and I judged that a plain duplication rather than a simp-interface defect.

findings.declaration: cubicSymbol_omega_norm (use of cubicSymbol_one_lower; lemma lives in CubicGram/Reciprocity.lean)
findings.problem: `cubicSymbol_one_lower : cubicSymbol 1 v = 1` is an unconditional, terminating rewrite to a normal form. It is not tagged `@[simp]`, although it is proved by `simp [cubicSymbol]`. Every caller therefore has to name it in `simp`/`norm_num`/`simp only` argument lists or use `rw`. The target does this at line 137. The same pattern appears in Reciprocity.lean (`simp only [cubicSymbol_one_lower]`, `simp only [map_one, cubicSymbol_one_lower, star_one]`, `simp only [cubicSymbol_one_lower, one_pow, star_one]`) and in MixedPoisson.lean (`rw [cubicSymbol_one_lower, one_pow]`). `simp` cannot discharge the base case of any primary-induction proof about `cubicSymbol` unless the lemma is supplied by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `cubicSymbol_one_lower` with `@[simp]` at its declaration in CubicGram/Reciprocity.lean. The left-hand side `cubicSymbol 1 v` has the specific head `cubicSymbol` and literal `1` and rewrites to `1`, so it cannot loop. After that, line 137 can drop it from the argument list, leaving something like `norm_num [normNat_of_isUnit isUnit_one]`. The `simp only [cubicSymbol_one_lower, ...]` base cases elsewhere could become plain `simp`. Before committing, check that tagging does not change the `cubicSymbol` simp sets of downstream files.
findings.benefit: The `cubicSymbol 1 v = 1` base case of the `primary_induction` proofs would be handled by plain `simp`. The explicit lemma lists in this file and in Reciprocity.lean and MixedPoisson.lean would get shorter, and future proofs would not need to know the lemma's name.

evidence.excerpt:
lemma cubicSymbol_one_lower (v : Eisenstein) : cubicSymbol 1 v = 1 := by
  simp [cubicSymbol]
